scenes.title: Aaron Beck and patient mapping a split-second automatic thought onto a two-column consulting-room notepad
scenes.era: 1963, University of Pennsylvania psychiatric consulting office, Philadelphia

layout.description: Sunlit 1963 wood-and-bookcase university consulting office where Beck moved the chair away from the psychoanalytic couch so doctor and patient sit face-to-face across a warm walnut desk over a two-column lined legal pad.

positions.who: Aaron T. Beck (mannequin in 1960s tweed sport coat, white shirt, and bow tie)
positions.where: seated across the walnut desk leaning forward collaboratively with a fountain pen over a divided legal pad

positions.who: Patient mannequin (in 1960s wool cardigan and collared shirt)
positions.where: seated upright in the armchair opposite the empty leather couch, pointing to the left column where the sudden automatic thought was just written

props.name: empty psychoanalytic couch in background
props.period_detail: classic tufted leather couch sitting unused against the bookshelf wall
props.physical_behavior: marks the historic shift from free-association couch to face-to-face empirical testing

props.name: two-column lined legal pad
props.period_detail: yellow 1960s legal pad ruled down the middle into 'Automatic Thought' on the left and 'Objective Evidence' on the right
props.physical_behavior: fills with concrete counter-evidence in the right column

props.name: cognitive triad triangle sketch
props.period_detail: clean index card showing a triangle labeled Self — World — Future

actions.verb_sequence: slumps shoulders recalling a silent hallway snub -> pauses as Beck slides the legal pad forward -> points as the hidden sentence goes down in the left column
draws a vertical line down the page -> writes three factual counter-examples in the right column

reactions.reaction: straightens posture visibly as the unexamined doom sentence shrinks beside real evidence

scenes.wardrobe: Beck: 1963 tweed jacket, crisp white shirt, classic bow tie. Patient: early-1960s knit cardigan over buttoned shirt and slacks.
scenes.lighting: Warm, high-key afternoon window daylight across walnut desk, books, and yellow legal pad.
scenes.recognition_hook: Leaving the Freudian couch empty behind them, Aaron Beck draws a single line down a notepad to test a patient's split-second 'automatic thought' against real facts.

key_visual.description: a 1960s psychiatrist in a bow tie and tweed jacket sitting face-to-face with a patient across a walnut desk writing on a two-column pad in front of an unused couch

scenes.title: Hallway pass-by triggering an arbitrary inference

layout.description: Bright office corridor where a hurried colleague checks a wristwatch and walks past without waving.

positions.where: standing by the hallway wall watching a hurried coworker rush past looking at a wristwatch

props.name: colleague's wristwatch & stack of files
props.period_detail: visible cue showing the coworker is simply late for a meeting
props.physical_behavior: missed entirely by selective negative interpretation

actions.verb_sequence: glances at wristwatch and rushes down hall -> Patient mannequin freezes and lowers gaze

reactions.reaction: interprets ordinary haste as personal rejection

scenes.recognition_hook: A coworker rushing late to a meeting becomes 'everyone thinks I'm incompetent' in half a second.

scenes.title: Comparing 50 depressed vs 31 control interview folders

layout.description: Desk stacked neatly with two labeled groups of manila clinical transcript folders (50 vs 31).

positions.where: highlighting recurring distortion patterns across open transcript pages

props.name: manila case transcript folders
props.physical_behavior: reveal arbitrary inference and overgeneralization across all 50 depressed records

actions.verb_sequence: circles matching Self-World-Future phrases across separate patient transcripts

reactions.reaction: sets aside the disproven Freudian hostility tally sheet

scenes.recognition_hook: Fifty patient transcripts disproved Beck's own Freudian hypothesis and exposed five repeatable thinking traps.

scenes.title: Modern two-column notebook check after an unanswered text

layout.description: Sunlit café table with a pocket notebook open beside a silent smartphone.

positions.where: writing 'Guess vs Fact' in a small pocket notebook

props.name: pocket notebook and pen
props.period_detail: two crisp columns separating 'They hate me' from 'They are in Tuesday lab until 5'

actions.verb_sequence: jots three realistic reasons a friend hasn't texted back -> sets pen down calmly

reactions.reaction: relaxes shoulders and returns to reading

scenes.recognition_hook: Putting a scary guess on paper beside three boring alternative explanations activates your prefrontal auditor.
